In the game of racing, speed matters. The breeze ups are done for Monday’s Magic Millions Horses In Training Sale and the top five fastest horses all came from two drafts. TTR spoke to them about the fastest five.

Zac Purton ticked off 1100 wins on the Sha Tin turf with a double on Sunday night. Deep Field and Divine Prophet both sired doubles, while it was trainer Frankie Lor’s double with two long time losers that had everyone talking.

The Aga Khan Studs’ brilliant entire Daryz defended his G1 Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to become the first colt since Alleged to win France’s biggest race twice in succession. The two juvenile Group 1s on the card went to the fillies with Amusingly and Green Empress, while The Thoroughbred Racing Corporation had a banner day with two Group 1 victories.

Arrowfield sent Tides to Pinatubo to add speed and substance - the resulting filly, Global Goal, is now a G1 Flight Stakes winner. Her success offers the most revealing story from a Saturday that also brought a Snitzel stakes treble and another Group 1 for Maurice’s Cosmic Crusader.

G3 Breeders’ Plate victor Flying Houdini cost more than his stakes-winning full sister, but at $60,000, he was still great value. Now a debut Group 3 winner of $140,000, he has the whole world ahead of him.

Ace Stud purchased the top two lots at Saturday evening’s Arqana Arc Sale. Ace Stud paid €1.9 million for Sunday’s G1 Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe runner Bright Light (City Light), and €1.15 million for Group 3 winner Space Waltz. The sale recorded a record gross of €11.7 million.

Seven Grade 1 races were the highlight of the North American racing scene on Saturday. Arabian Crown won the G1 Canadian International Stakes giving Godolphin their fifth win in the race. The juveniles were out in force in America with Grade 1 winners for sires Into Mischief, War Of Will, Constitution and Tacitus.

Juddmonte’s Blue Bolt stayed unbeaten for this campaign and made it four Group 1 victories in succession when taking out Saturday’s G1 Sun Chariot Stakes. In France, Caballo De Mar had it back to back wins in the G1 Prix du Cadran, and Fairy Glen franked his Dubai form in the G1 Prix de Royallieu.
